title: An optimized protocol for phenotyping human granulocytes by mass cytometry
author: Vivanco Gonzalez, Oliveria, et al.

steps.title: Prepare reagents
steps.instruction: Make all solutions needed for the experiment and keep them under the specified conditions.

substeps.instruction: Combine 498 mL cold dPBS with 2 mL 0.5 M EDTA to obtain dPBS + 2 mM EDTA; filter through an Argos 0.22 µm filter, refrigerate, and use within 1 month.
Filter double‑distilled water through an Argos 0.22 µm filter and store at 4 °C until use.
Dilute BioLegend 10× RBC lysis buffer 1:10 with double‑distilled water to make 1× buffer; keep at 4 °C.
Prepare 0.5 mM cisplatin solution by adding 1 µL of 100 mM cisplatin in DMSO (stored at –20 °C) to 199 µL low‑barium PBS; keep at 4 °C (handle as hazardous).
Use 16 % PFA that has been opened ≤1 month and stored sealed at 20‑23 °C; 1 mL will be needed per 1 mL peripheral blood.
Prepare DNA intercalator solution on the day of intracellular staining (details not specified).
Warm RPMI‑1640 medium to 37 °C.
Make 2 µg/mL anti‑IgE in warm RPMI (2 µL anti‑IgE (1 mg/mL) + 1 mL RPMI) and 4 ng/mL IL‑3 in warm RPMI (1 µL IL‑3 (4 ng/µL) + 1 mL RPMI); keep both at 37 °C until use.

steps.title: Block and stain surface markers
steps.instruction: Perform Fc block and surface antibody staining on up to 10 million cells per tube.

substeps.instruction: Add 2.5 µL Human TruStain FcX to each tube and tap to dissolve cells.
Incubate 10 min at 20‑23 °C.
Add 52.5 µL surface antibody cocktail (bringing total volume to 100 µL).
Tap to resuspend and prevent clumps.
Incubate 30 min at 20‑23 °C.

steps.title: Cisplatin staining and fixation
steps.instruction: Label dead cells with cisplatin, then fix cells with PFA using CSM buffer washes.

substeps.instruction: Add 899 µL low‑barium PBS and 1 µL 0.5 mM cisplatin to each tube (final 0.5 µM cisplatin, 1 mL total).
Vortex briefly and incubate 5 min at 20‑23 °C.
Add 4 mL CSM, centrifuge 250 × g 5 min, aspirate supernatant leaving ≈100 µL, and tap to resuspend.
Repeat the vortex/incubate and CSM‑wash step (steps above).
Add 900 µL CSM and 100 µL 16 % PFA (final 1.5 % PFA).
Incubate 10 min at 20‑23 °C.
Centrifuge 500 × g 5 min at 4 °C, aspirate supernatant leaving ≈100 µL, and tap to resuspend.
Add 4 mL CSM, centrifuge 500 × g 5 min at 4 °C, aspirate supernatant leaving ≈100 µL.
Pause point: fixed cells may remain in CSM at 4 °C for up to 24 h.

steps.title: Permeabilize and intracellular staining
steps.instruction: Permeabilize cells with methanol, stain intracellular antigens, and incubate with DNA intercalator.

substeps.instruction: Tap tubes to resuspend pellet, add 1 mL 4 °C 100 % MeOH, incubate on ice exactly 10 min.
Add 3 mL CSM to stop permeabilization.
Centrifuge 500 × g 5 min at 4 °C, aspirate supernatant leaving ≈100 µL.
Resuspend pellet by tapping and repeat the MeOH‑incubation and CSM‑stop steps once more.
Aspirate supernatant and adjust volume to 65 µL for intracellular staining.
Add 35 µL intracellular antibody cocktail (total volume 100 µL).
Incubate 30 min at 20‑23 °C.
Add 3 mL CSM, centrifuge 500 × g 5 min at 4 °C, aspirate supernatant leaving ≈100 µL.
Resuspend pellet by tapping, add 900 µL DNA intercalator solution (total 1 mL), mix gently by pipetting.
Incubate at 4 °C for ≥16 h (or 20 min at 20‑23 °C if running the same day, then keep at 4 °C).
Pause point: cells in DNA intercalator can be stored at 4 °C for up to 1 week before CyTOF.

steps.title: Prepare samples for CyTOF acquisition
steps.instruction: Wash cells, add calibration beads, and filter before acquisition.

substeps.instruction: Add 4 mL CSM (4 °C) to each tube, tap to resuspend.
Centrifuge 500 × g 5 min at 4 °C, aspirate supernatant leaving ≈100 µL.
Resuspend pellet, add 4 mL filtered double‑distilled water.
Centrifuge 500 × g 5 min at 4 °C, aspirate supernatant leaving ≈100 µL.
Repeat the water‑wash (add 4 mL water, centrifuge, aspirate).
Dilute EQ Four‑Element Calibration Beads 10‑fold in filtered double‑distilled water (e.g., 2.5 mL beads + 22.5 mL water) and keep at 4 °C.
Count cells with a hemacytometer.
Immediately before analysis, tap to resuspend and add diluted EQ beads to achieve 1 × 10⁶ cells / mL.
Filter the sample through a Falcon round‑bottom tube with a 35 µm cell strainer.
Acquire at ≤500 events / s; if rate is higher, dilute further with EQ‑bead/water mixture.
Keep samples on ice until acquisition.

steps.title: Process CyTOF data
steps.instruction: Normalize, transform, and analyze the acquired CyTOF data.

substeps.instruction: Run FCS files through MATLAB‑based bead‑normalization software (Finck et al., 2013).
Upload normalized files to Cytobank for gating (see Vivanco Gonzalez et al., 2020 Fig 1A for gating scheme).
Quantile‑normalize protein expression per donor using R.
Apply arcsinh transformation with cofactor 5.
Perform dimensionality reduction (t‑SNE) and Leiden clustering using Scanpy (Python).
